text:
Overall quality score: **5/10**.

The code is readable and the happy path is covered, but I would not call it production-ready. The main risks are ingestion correctness and resilience: stale data is retained, bad-but-valid input can crash the process, required identifiers are not validated, and ingestion is not atomic.

Verification run: `python -m pytest -q` passed `6/6`; bytecode compilation passed when pycache output was redirected outside the read-only workspace.

| Severity | File / Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:98) `98-104` | `ingest()` clears warnings/stats but never clears `results`, so re-ingesting a changed input directory leaves stale rows. |
| high | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:103) `103-104`, [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:405) `405-438` | Ingestion commits per row, so a mid-ingest failure can leave a partially updated database. |
| high | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:172) `172-176`, [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:215) `215-219`, [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:255) `255-259` | Blank `run_id`, `model`, and `task` values are accepted; blank IDs collide and overwrite prior rows. |
| medium | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:191) `191-199` | Harness B assumes each JSONL value and `metrics` are dicts; valid JSON arrays/scalars or string metrics crash ingestion. |
| medium | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:228) `228-230` | Malformed XML is not caught, so `results.xml` parse errors crash instead of being recorded as warnings. |
| medium | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:268) `268-312` | Non-finite scores are mishandled; `nan` reaches SQLite and crashes, while infinities are silently clamped. |
| medium | [evalmerge/pipeline.py](/work/evalmerge/pipeline.py:143) `143-156` | Harness A reads columns positionally and ignores the header, so reordered or wrong CSV headers silently corrupt data. |
| medium | [generate_fixtures.py](/work/generate_fixtures.py:21) `21-22` | Fixture generation recursively deletes any existing target path without a safety guard. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change scope: **~180 LOC**. Most of that is centralizing row validation, making ingestion snapshot/transaction semantics explicit, hardening parsers, and adding negative tests.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this as-is in a PR review.**
